decision_question: Should we invest in or develop a strategic position in nuclear fusion technology now, or wait for further de-risking?

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nuclear fusion will not achieve grid-connected electricity before 2035.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, near-term investment in fusion is premature; focus on fission and renewables.
needed_evidence: Published timelines from major projects (ITER, SPARC, DEMO) and independent assessments.

hypotheses.hypothesis: First-of-a-kind fusion plants will have LCOE > $100/MWh, making them uncompetitive without subsidies.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Determines if fusion can compete with renewables and gas in the 2030s.
needed_evidence: LCOE estimates from credible sources (IEA, Lazard, fusion companies).
search_queries: Lazard levelized cost of energy fusion

hypotheses.hypothesis: Private fusion companies have raised over $5 billion cumulatively, but less than 20% is from non-dilutive sources.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Indicates reliance on venture capital; risk of funding gaps.
needed_evidence: Aggregate funding data from Fusion Industry Association, Crunchbase.

hypotheses.hypothesis: No fusion reactor has achieved a net energy gain (Q>1) for more than 5 seconds.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, sustained operation remains a major hurdle.
needed_evidence: Records from NIF, JET, and other experiments.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Government funding for fusion (e.g., US, EU, Japan, China) exceeds $2 billion annually, but is concentrated in ITER.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Shows public sector commitment and potential for policy risk.
needed_evidence: Budget documents from DOE, Euratom, etc.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The number of fusion startups has plateaued since 2020, indicating consolidation or disillusionment.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Market maturity signal; affects competitive dynamics.
needed_evidence: Count of active fusion companies over time.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fusion will first be commercialized for marine propulsion or industrial heat, not electricity.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: Changes addressable market and investment thesis.

chart_data_needs.title: Fusion LCOE vs. Other Technologies (2024-2050)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: When will fusion become cost-competitive with renewables and gas?
comparison_set: Solar PV, Onshore Wind, Gas Combined Cycle, Nuclear Fission, Fusion
preferred_sources: Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy Analysis
search_queries: Lazard LCOE 2024 solar wind gas nuclear
IEA World Energy Outlook 2024 LCOE fusion
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use Lazard's published LCOE ranges for comparators. For fusion, use only publicly stated targets from companies or industry associations. If only two endpoints exist, interpolate using a CAGR assumption and mark as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Establishes the economic hurdle for fusion adoption by comparing projected LCOE ranges with established technologies over time.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before showing this chart, the report argues that fusion's commercial viability hinges on cost competitiveness. The audience needs to see how fusion's projected costs compare with alternatives across a multi-decade horizon.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Fusion LCOE remains above $100/MWh until at least 2040, while solar and wind fall below $30/MWh, indicating fusion will require subsidies or carbon pricing to compete.

chart_data_needs.title: Fusion Funding Landscape: Public vs. Private (2010-2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Who is paying for fusion development and how has the funding mix evolved?
comparison_set: Public funding (government budgets, ITER), Private funding (venture capital, corporate)
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use FIA data as primary; cross-check with Crunchbase for private totals. If exact annual figures unavailable, use linear interpolation between known data points and note as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows the trend in total annual fusion funding split by public and private sources, highlighting the dominance of public (ITER) funding and recent private surge.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report discusses the capital intensity of fusion. The audience needs to see the scale and sources of investment to assess financial momentum and risk.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Private fusion funding has grown from near zero in 2010 to over $1B annually by 2024, but public funding (mainly ITER) still accounts for ~60% of total, indicating continued government dependence.

chart_data_needs.title: Fusion Reactor Net Energy Gain Duration (Q>1)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How close are fusion experiments to sustained net energy production?
comparison_set: JET, NIF, EAST, KSTAR, SPARC (planned), ITER (planned)
search_queries: JET fusion record 2023 Q value duration
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use only published experimental results. For planned experiments (SPARC, ITER), use design targets and mark as projections. Bubble size represents duration on log scale.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Visualizes the progress in fusion energy gain (Q) and pulse duration, showing that no experiment has achieved sustained Q>1 for more than a few seconds.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report explains the Q>1 milestone. The audience needs to see the gap between current records and commercial requirements (hours of sustained operation).
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: The best fusion experiments achieve Q>1 for only seconds, far from the hours needed for commercial plants, indicating a decade-plus of engineering work remains.

chart_data_needs.title: Global Electricity Generation and Potential Fusion Share (2024-2050)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: What is the addressable market for fusion under different adoption scenarios?
comparison_set: Total global electricity generation, Fusion optimistic scenario, Fusion pessimistic scenario
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use IEA data for total generation. For fusion share, use only published scenarios from credible sources. If only two scenarios exist, interpolate linearly and mark as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Quantifies the potential fusion electricity generation in TWh under optimistic and pessimistic scenarios, overlaid on total global electricity generation.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report discusses market size. The audience needs to see the range of possible fusion output to assess revenue potential.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Even under optimistic scenarios, fusion provides less than 5% of global electricity by 2050, limiting near-term market impact.

chart_data_needs.title: Adoption Funnel: Utility Interest in Fusion (2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: What is the conversion rate from utility awareness to commercial orders for fusion?
preferred_sources: Utility surveys (e.g., Utility Dive, S&P Global)
Company press releases on pilot projects
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use survey data if available; otherwise, use expert estimates from industry reports. Mark any assumed conversion rates as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows the drop-off at each stage of the adoption funnel, highlighting the gap between interest and actual procurement.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report discusses market adoption. The audience needs to see how many utilities are actively considering fusion versus placing orders.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: While 60% of utilities are aware of fusion, only 5% have signed pilot agreements, and none have placed commercial orders, indicating a long adoption cycle.

chart_data_needs.title: Timeline of Major Fusion Milestones and Delays
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How credible are current fusion commercialization timelines given historical delays?
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use official project updates. For projects with multiple revisions, use the most recent publicly stated date. Mark any unconfirmed dates as 'planned'.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Plots planned vs. actual milestones for major fusion projects, showing a pattern of delays that undermines confidence in current schedules.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report discusses technology readiness. The audience needs to see the track record of delays to assess the risk of timeline slippage.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Every major fusion project has experienced multi-year delays; ITER is now 10+ years behind original schedule, suggesting current 2035-2040 commercial targets are optimistic.

chart_data_needs.title: Fusion Startup Count Over Time (2010-2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Is the fusion startup ecosystem growing or consolidating?
preferred_sources: Fusion Industry Association annual member list
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use FIA membership as proxy for active startups. Cross-check with Crunchbase for completeness. If annual data missing, interpolate linearly and mark as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows the number of active fusion startups annually, indicating market entry and exit trends.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before this chart, the report discusses competitive landscape. The audience needs to see whether the number of players is increasing or plateauing.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: The number of fusion startups grew rapidly from 2010 to 2020 but has plateaued around 40 since 2021, suggesting consolidation or a slowdown in new entrants.
